# Test files allowed to be absent from some platforms (ini-2x8.8).
#
#   <repo-relative test file>  <goos>[,<goos>...]  # reason
#
# Enforced by `go run ./scripts/testcensus`, which runs in `make check` and in
# CI. Any OTHER cross-platform difference fails the build.
#
# THE REASON FIELD IS MANDATORY AND IS THE POINT. This project hit the same
# class four times: one file legitimately needs a constraint, a portable symbol
# is parked in it, and every consumer inherits the constraint until whole suites
# have left a platform with nobody choosing it. An exemption without a stated
# reason is that same accident, written down and blessed. If you cannot say why
# a file cannot compile somewhere, the honest move is to find out, not to add a
# line here.
#
# Before adding an entry, check the constraint has not simply PROPAGATED: if the
# file only needs the tag because it uses a helper or const defined in a tagged
# sibling, move the portable half into an untagged file instead. That is what
# ini-47w did, and it returned two whole suites to Windows.
#
# SEEDED FROM A REAL RUN, 2026-08-12 (ini-2x8.8), then AUDITED (ini-2x8.9): each
# entry whose rationale had never been recorded was tested by removing its tag
# and compiling for Windows. Three files turned out not to need the constraint
# at all and are gone from this list; the rest carry the compiler error or the
# specific incompatible call as their reason.
#
# ONE OF THE SEEDED REASONS WAS WRONG, and it is worth knowing why. This file
# briefly claimed window_server_test.go was constrained because it "serves the
# pane stream over a unix-domain socket". It does not -- it binds TCP on
# 127.0.0.1, and the file's own header comment says "none of these tests bind a
# unix socket". The reason had been INFERRED from a grep hit on that very
# comment rather than read. An inferred reason is not evidence, and it lands in
# the same place as an invented one: a plausible sentence guarding a gap nobody
# has actually checked. Read the file.

# ── Drive a real PTY (creack/pty is Unix-only in this usage) ──────────
internal/tui/attention_emitter_probe_test.go  windows  # live OSC 777 probe spawns a real Claude Code under a PTY via creack/pty
internal/tui/notif_channel_probe_test.go      windows  # live notification-channel matrix spawns a real Claude Code under a PTY via creack/pty; its portable half (screen render, silence diagnosis) lives untagged in notif_probe_diagnosis_test.go
internal/tui/census_zerochange_test.go        windows  # builds and runs the real binary under a PTY to capture the startup census
internal/tui/rolesless_boot_test.go           windows  # boots the real binary under a PTY

# ── Construct real panes, which own a PTY ────────────────────────────
internal/tui/altscreen_probe_test.go          windows  # NewPane starts a PTY-backed child process
internal/tui/altscreen_live_vim_test.go       windows  # NewPane starts a PTY-backed child process (drives real vim)
internal/tui/clickbadge_live_test.go          windows  # NewPane starts a PTY-backed child process
internal/tui/liveregion_probe_test.go         windows  # NewPane starts a PTY-backed child process

# ── Unix-only OS surfaces ────────────────────────────────────────────
internal/config/config_perms_unix_test.go     windows  # asserts 0600 file modes and Chmod semantics that Windows does not implement
internal/tui/foldback_test.go                 windows  # unix-domain socket plumbing plus syscall-level process control
internal/tui/window_wedge_test.go             windows  # unix-domain socket plumbing plus syscall-level process control
internal/roles/selector_goroutine_test.go     windows  # opens /dev/tty directly
internal/roles/qa_ini4pk1_test.go             windows  # opens /dev/tty directly
internal/tui/battery_darwin_test.go           linux,windows  # parses `pmset` output; the source file it covers is //go:build darwin

# ── Audited: constraint is REAL, with the evidence that proves it ────
# ini-2x8.9 removed each tag and compiled for Windows. These failed, and the
# compiler error IS the reason -- the symbol they test does not exist there.
internal/roles/selector_test.go               windows  # undefined: selectorState -- selector.go is itself //go:build !windows, so the raw-terminal selector does not exist on Windows
internal/roles/selector_unit_test.go          windows  # undefined: buildDisplayRows -- same: the symbol under test lives in the //go:build !windows selector.go

# ── Compiles for Windows, but MEASURED to hang there ─────────────────
# ini-2x8.9 unmasked these on the strength of a COMPILE check and CI proved the
# compile check insufficient, exactly as that bead warned it might be. The tui
# package timed out at 600s on windows-latest (run 31651424793, job 94296390977)
# with goroutines parked in startWindowServer's TCP Accept and in drainEmulator's
# emulator Read. Re-tagged on evidence, not on retreat. Whether the window server
# itself works on Windows is a PRODUCT question, filed separately -- these tests
# hanging is the symptom, not the whole finding.
internal/tui/window_server_test.go            windows  # tui package hangs 600s on windows CI: goroutines stuck in startWindowServer TCP Accept (run 31651424793)
internal/tui/protocol_version_test.go         windows  # drives window_server_test.go's startTestWindowServer, which hangs the tui package on windows CI (run 31651424793); the portable half lives untagged in protocol_version_portable_test.go
internal/tui/qodm_starts_fresh_test.go        windows  # composed two-process retirement check: drives startTestWindowServer plus a real viewer under a PTY (creack/pty), both unavailable on the windows leg
internal/tui/parity_test.go                   windows  # same hang: depends on startTestWindowServer, which is what parks in Accept

# ── Compiles for Windows, but RUNTIME portability is genuinely doubtful ───
# Stated rather than resolved by guesswork, per ini-2x8.9's AC. The compile-time
# constraint here is inherited (buildInitechBinary is portable Go), but the file
# builds the real binary as "initech" with no extension and then executes it,
# and Windows generally requires .exe to exec. Unmasking it without making
# buildInitechBinary platform-aware would trade a silent gap for a red CI leg
# that tells us nothing new. Candidate for its own bead.
internal/tui/window_cli_integration_test.go   windows  # inherited from buildInitechBinary (portable), but the test EXECUTES a binary built without a .exe suffix; runtime portability unverified

# ── ini-6m4 composed acceptance rig ───
# Genuine constraint, not propagation: the rig spawns two real initech windows
# under PTYs (creack/pty, unix-only master API) and probes process liveness via
# syscall.Signal(0). The unit halves of every guard it composes are in the
# UNTAGGED viewer_parity_test.go / viewer_plan_test.go and run on all three
# platforms; this file adds only the live two-window composition.
internal/tui/sixm4_rig_test.go                windows  # PTY rig (creack/pty + signal-0 liveness probe); portable guard halves live untagged in viewer_parity_test.go

# ── ini-9imx triage rig ───
# Genuine constraint: spawns real PTY processes (creack/pty via NewPane's unix
# path) to measure message fate against a really-suspended pane. Findings
# generator, gated INITECH_9IMX=1; its DirectSendText leg fails by design
# while the bypass loss is open.
internal/tui/suspend_fate_rig_test.go        windows  # real-PTY suspension fate rig (gated INITECH_9IMX=1)
